objectives.title: Read the flag
objectives.prompt: With only a username list, AS-REP roast the account whose Kerberos pre-authentication is disabled, crack its AS-REP hash offline to recover the password, then read flag.txt from the //dc/imaging share that only that account may open.
hints: The real-world technique needs no credentials, only usernames: an account with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled makes the KDC return an AS-REP to an unauthenticated request. Point your resolver and /etc/krb5.conf at the DC, then roast the list: GetNPUsers.py LAKESIDE.LAB/ -usersfile users.txt -no-pass -dc-ip <dc> -format john. Only svc-scanner is flagged DONT_REQ_PREAUTH.

This is a modern DC with RC4 disabled, so the AS-REP comes back AES (`$krb5asrep$18$...`). Crack it with John: `john --format=krb5asrep --wordlist=rockyou.txt asrep.hash`. hashcat's `-m 18200` only understands the older RC4 (`$krb5asrep$23$`) form, so it will not take this hash.
The password is a weak word built from the scanner service's name and a year. Once cracked: smbclient //dc/imaging -U 'LAKESIDE\svc-scanner%<cracked>' -c 'get flag.txt'.

steps.title: Name the technique
steps.prompt: What is the name of the attack that recovers a password offline from the Kerberos AS-REP of an account that does not require pre-authentication?

steps.title: Find the roastable account
steps.prompt: Which account has Kerberos pre-authentication disabled and is therefore AS-REP roastable? (username)

steps.title: Name the UAC flag
steps.prompt: Which userAccountControl flag, when set on an account, makes it AS-REP roastable? (its name)

steps.title: Name the ticket encryption
steps.prompt: Which encryption type is this modern DC's AS-REP, the one john cracks here? (name or Kerberos etype number)

steps.title: Pick the cracking tool
steps.prompt: Which John the Ripper format cracks this AES AS-REP ($krb5asrep$18$) hash?
